top_stories.title: DSS to hold rallies on June 16 seeking Karnataka Cabinet berth for H.C. Mahadevappa - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Dalit Sangharsha Samiti**, a Karnataka-based organization, announced a statewide rally on June 16th to demand a Cabinet berth for **H.C. Mahadevappa**, a senior Congress leader and former Minister. The group highlighted **Mahadevappa's** contributions to Dalit welfare and social justice during his tenure as Minister, citing specific initiatives like securing funds for the Dr B.R. Ambedkar Bhavan and strengthening enforcement of laws against atrocities against Scheduled Castes. They urged the state Congress leadership to accommodate **Mahadevappa** in the next Cabinet expansion and provide adequate representation for Dalits in other positions of power.

top_stories.title: Two held for posing as Kala Jathedi gang members to issue extortion threat to Delhi businessman - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Delhi Police** arrested two Haryana-based businessmen, Rajan Kalra (26) and Sahil Garg (38), for allegedly impersonating members of the notorious Kala Jathedi gang and extorting money from a Delhi businessman.  The accused used international and Indian phone numbers to threaten Rohit Jain, who had an ongoing dispute with Garg over a disputed ₹2.95 crore payment. **Police** recovered two mobile phones from Kalra and another from Garg during raids in Haryana. The case was registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for extortion and criminal intimidation.

top_stories.title: Security forces recover huge cache of arms, ammunition from Maoist dump in Odisha's Malkangiri - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Security forces** in Odisha and Chhattisgarh recovered a large cache of weapons, explosives, and equipment from a Maoist dump. The items included an INSAS light machine gun, two INSAS rifles, tiffin bombs, IEDs, and other materials.  The **District Voluntary Force (DVF)** and **Border Security Force (BSF)** conducted the search operation based on information provided by surrendered Maoists. This seizure is considered a significant blow to the insurgency's destructive activities in the region.

top_stories.title: Anbumani meets T.N. CM Vijay, urges caste-based survey announcement in Governor’s address - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Anbumani Ramadoss**, leader of the **Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK)**, met with **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** in Chennai to urge the state government to announce a caste-based survey during the Governor’s address on June 18th.  Mr. Ramadoss stated that the resolution passed at a multi-party meeting last week, which included representatives from 42 political parties and organizations, unanimously supported conducting a caste-based survey in Tamil Nadu. He argued that the existing reservation policies were based on outdated data collected during the British period and that a modern survey would provide accurate socio-economic and educational details of the state's population.

top_stories.title: Threats Against Politicians Skyrocketed After Meta Changed Its Speech Rules | WIRED
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Meta** overhauled its content moderation rules last year, claiming to relax restrictions and promote free speech.  A new report from the Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) found that abusive and racist comments targeting lawmakers tripled in the six months after the changes. The report also documented a significant increase in threats against President Trump and other hateful content. While **Meta** maintains its decision was driven by free speech principles, experts argue that relaxing moderation has led to an amplification of harmful content, potentially contributing to increased political violence and harassment.

top_stories.title: T.N. govt. must ensure senior citizens are provided safe shelter, food, and medical care: Tamilisai Soundararajan - The Hindu
top_stories.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan**, BJP leader, expressed deep concern over the suicides of three elderly persons in Namakkal and urged **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to address the issue by identifying vulnerable seniors and providing them with support services.  She called for government action to ensure adequate care, including shelter, food, medical attention, and emotional assistance. Soundararajan also highlighted the importance of protecting senior citizens' dignity and well-being.

top_stories.title: Asteroid alert! NASA tracks two aeroplane-sized asteroids passing Earth today; know if they pose any risk | - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **NASA** and other space agencies are tracking two near-Earth objects, 2026 LD and 2026 KM3, as they pass Earth at distances measured in millions of kilometers. While these objects are described as "aeroplane-sized," their flybys are routine encounters within the safe, non-threatening range classified by planetary defense systems.  The tracking itself is crucial for refining orbital models and predicting asteroid trajectories years or even decades ahead.

top_stories.title: UK to deploy AI legal assistants in Crown courts to tackle record case backlog | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **UK government** will trial artificial intelligence-powered legal assistants in Crown Courts to address a record backlog of criminal cases.  **Justice Secretary David Lammy** plans to announce the initiative at London Tech Week, highlighting AI's potential to modernize the justice system and deliver faster outcomes for victims. The technology is expected to analyze case files, identify cases ready for trial, and group similar hearings together. Legal bodies have welcomed the pilot but stressed the importance of thorough evaluation and investment in courts and staffing.

top_stories.title: Torso of unidentified man found in suitcase at Chennai’s Perambur railway station - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Government Railway Police (GRP)** in Chennai are investigating the discovery of a mutilated torso inside a suitcase at Perambur railway station. The victim's identity remains unknown, and police are working to establish it. Commuters alerted authorities after detecting a foul smell from the bag near Platform No. 4 around 7:15 a.m.

top_stories.title: More than bones: German students buried their classroom skeleton after discovering it was a real person, likely from India | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: In Schleiden, Germany, a skeleton that had been used as a teaching aid in a biology classroom for decades was recently buried after students discovered it likely originated from India. The discovery led to an investigation into the forgotten global trade of human skeletons that supplied anatomical specimens to institutions across Europe and North America during the 19th and 20th centuries.  The trade, fueled by the growing demand for real human remains in medical education, was largely unregulated and often involved individuals who died from ordinary causes without clear consent or documentation. The skeleton's journey highlights ethical concerns surrounding the use of human remains in educational settings and raises questions about ownership, consent, and the treatment of the dead.
